text.p: Northern Telecom Ltd is mulling selling off bits of some non-core businesses in an effort to set up an affiliate structure along the lines of that of networking rival Newbridge Networks Corp.

"We definitely have a view that there are certain businesses that we have today, while they're strong, could be stronger if they were managed differently -- with partners, as opposed to owned by Northern Telecom," Nortel chief executive Jean Monty said in a recent interview.
"Probably in bigger chunks than Newbridge. The concept is pretty well the same, but bigger chunks," he added.
Nortel last month spun off 25 percent of its Secure Networks unit, Entrust, to an investment group of five companies. The group paid about US$26 million for the stake.

"(There are) units that are inside Nortel that are basically complements to the offerings we give customers but not necessarily core to the competency we are trying to build for the long-term...the networking competency," Monty said.

"The intent would be to...downgrade them to a subsidiary, maybe to affiliates, maybe to investments. In one case we will keep 70 percent, in another case we will keep 60 percent, in another case we will only keep 30 percent," he added.
The timing of such spinoffs remains up in the air, Monty said. But he added that they offered a way to galvanize management at certain units and to raise cash without the dilution of an equity issue.
Newbridge chief executive Terry Matthews swears by the affiliate structure, which is loosely modeled on a Japanese system.
He has said the design served to keep Newbridge in touch with fledgling technologies and build on existing products.
